focal_basis: max(1.5 x worst held-out focal miss, 5.0 cm3 floor), both measured as the largest component surviving a max(1.5 mm, one voxel) shave, as the scorer measures a submission; shave 1.5 mm here, worst held-out miss 0.47 cm3
dura_basis: Recalibrated for the HD-BET + SynthStrip(-b -2) + ANTs(INV2) panel. The reference consensus reaches 15.2-33.7 cm3 beyond the pial envelope across the three subjects, so the cap must exceed 33.7 for the ground truth to pass its own gate; it must stay below 117.7, the smallest over-envelope volume among masks the gate exists to reject (SynthStrip at its default border, 117.7-194.8 cm3 across subjects). 50 cm3 gives the reference about 48% headroom inside that window. Deliberately tighter than the widest single panel member (ANTs at 33.2-73.1 cm3): a panel member is one opinion used to form the consensus, not a model answer, and the task asks for a mask with the dura removed.
prompt: Skull-strip the 7T MP2RAGE image of sub-075 (ds003642, OpenNeuro) AND remove the dura, producing a brain-extracted image and a binary brain mask in the input's native space.
focal_bg_basis: max(1.5 x worst legitimate non-panel inclusion, 10 cm3 backstop). Measured on every non-panel mask available: well-chosen invocations (HD-BET and SynthStrip at defaults, BET -R, BET default on paediatric) admit 0.00-3.87 cm3, while BET at its defaults on motion-corrupted T1w admits 16.67-113.27 cm3. The cap sits in the empty band between them. It is deliberately looser than the core cap: lost brain is unrecoverable, whereas retained skull is visible and downstream-recoverable, so the gate catches only gross inclusion and bg_fp_frac_of_ref (weight 0.20) prices the gradient. Evidence is thin -- 16 legitimate masks from three tasks, none over-inclusive for 3T, stroke or diffusion.
